subject.title: fix(gateway): reject unsafe explicit approval IDs

question: Should OpenClaw make the new 1–128-character ASCII approval-ID format the enforced gateway contract for all existing explicit-ID callers?
rationale: This is a deliberate security hardening boundary, but it narrows input accepted by externally connected gateway clients and cannot be safely treated as a purely internal refactor.

options.title: Approve the bounded identifier contract
options.body: Merge the shared validation after exact-head proof confirms legitimate producer and external-client compatibility.

options.title: Preserve a broader compatible contract
options.body: Revise the boundary or add a documented migration path if existing supported clients require additional identifier characters.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded identifier contract
recommendation.body: Merge the shared validation after exact-head proof confirms legitimate producer and external-client compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged approval-lifecycle feature and this focused contract-hardening follow-up.
